A.why: The suggestion system rewarding cost reduction is the Initiative example (F3), but the stem also describes the 'we' practice, so Initiative covers only half of the practice.

B.why: Replacing 'I' with 'We' is the Esprit de corps example (F3), but the suggestion-reward half is Initiative.

C.why: Nothing in the stem or F3 links either practice to unity of direction.

D.why: Nothing in the stem or F3 links either practice to centralisation.

items.missing_decisive_condition: The stem describes two practices belonging to two different principles (Initiative and Esprit de corps) and asks for one principle; which practice is meant is not stated.
items.syllabus_fit: Fair chapter, but the stem is double-barrelled.
items.quality_note: Two defensible answers (A and B); should name only one practice.
items.source_explanation: F3 ties the employee suggestion system rewarding cost reduction to Initiative and replacing 'I' with 'We' to Esprit de corps. The stem contains both, so A and B are each partly correct and there is no single answer. C and D are unsupported by F3.

A.why: F15 says debt is cheaper and likely lowers overall cost of capital if cost of equity is unaffected.

B.why: F15: likely to lower overall cost of capital; fixed financial charges and financial risk increase.

C.why: F15: payment of interest and return of principal is obligatory, so risk rises.

D.why: F15 says higher debt increases financial risk; equity being riskless does not leave risk unchanged.

items.quality_note: Clear; distractors plausible and each contradicted by F15.
items.source_explanation: F15 states more debt is likely to lower overall cost of capital provided cost of equity is unaffected, but it raises fixed financial charges and financial risk. A reverses the cost claim. C contradicts the obligatory interest and principal payment. D contradicts that debt increases financial risk.

A.why: F20: appeal to the State Commission within forty five days from the date of order.

B.why: F20 gives forty five, not thirty.

C.why: F20 gives forty five, not sixty.

D.why: F20 gives forty five, not fifteen.

items.quality_note: Direct recall; clear stem, plausible distractors.
items.source_explanation: F20 states a party dissatisfied with the District Commission's order can appeal to the State Commission on facts or law within forty five days. The other periods are not what F20 states.

A.why: F12: education is broad knowledge and understanding; the stem describes a firm-run skills programme.

B.why: F12: development is learning opportunities for growth; the stem does not say growth of personality or potential is the aim.

C.why: Selection is not defined in F12 and is hiring, not a programme for existing employees.

D.why: F12: training increases skills for specific jobs, but the stem does not say the skills are for a specific job.

items.missing_decisive_condition: Whether the programme targets a specific current or intended job (training) or broader growth (development) is not stated; 'skills and knowledge' straddles training and education.
items.syllabus_fit: Fair chapter, but the concepts overlap per F12.
items.quality_note: Ambiguous; F12 itself says the terms overlap.
items.source_explanation: F12 defines training as improving skills for specific jobs, education as knowledge and understanding, and development as growth opportunities, and says they overlap. The stem gives no job-specific or growth cue, so Training and Development are both arguable. Selection is unrelated.

A.why: F1 (iii): planning in June, continuous monitoring and timely briefing illustrate coordination as a continuous process.

B.why: F1 (iv) all-pervasive concerns coordination at all levels and across departments; the stem shows continuity over time.

C.why: F1 says coordination is not a one-time function.

D.why: F1 says coordination is required at all levels.

items.syllabus_fit: Fair for Nature and Significance of Management.
items.quality_note: Close to textbook wording; distractors clear.
items.source_explanation: F1 (iii) uses the same Smita example for coordination as a continuous process, beginning at planning and continuing through monitoring. B concerns levels and departments (F1 iv), not shown here. C and D contradict F1.

A.why: F14: the manager deals only with significant deviations, saving time.

B.why: F14: management by exception facilitates delegation of authority.

C.why: F14 points 1 and 2: saves time and effort and focuses attention on important areas.

D.why: F14 point 3: it increases employee morale.

items.source_explanation: F14 lists saved time and effort and focus on important areas as advantages of dealing only with deviations beyond the permissible limit. A, B and D reverse F14's statements that time is saved, delegation is facilitated and morale rises.

A.why: Finance and power/water are inputs per F6.

B.why: Finance is an input per F6.

C.why: Power and water are inputs per F6.

D.why: F6 lists payment of taxes and return on financial investment as outputs.

items.quality_note: Clear; each distractor includes an input.
items.source_explanation: F6 lists finance, power and water as inputs, and goods and services, taxes to government and return on investment to investors as outputs. Hence (ii) and (iv) are outputs; A, B and C each include an input.

A.why: F10 (Davis): informal organisation is not established or required by the formal organisation.

B.why: Barnard (F10) says it may contribute to joint results, not only when it does.

D.why: Davis (F10): not established or required by the formal organisation, arising spontaneously as people associate.

items.source_explanation: F10: Davis describes spontaneous personal and social relations not established or required by the formal organisation; Barnard says without conscious purpose. A and C contradict this, and B turns Barnard's 'may contribute' into 'only when'.

A.why: 10,000 + 4 x 1,800 = 17,200, a time based salary plus performance incentive, matching F11's combination plan.

B.why: Total is 17,200 not 7,200, and it includes a time based part.

C.why: Ignores the Rs 4 per unit incentive; total is 17,200.

D.why: Amount right, but salary and incentive are direct financial payments (F11), not indirect like employer paid insurance.

items.quality_note: Clear calculation plus classification; distractors plausible.
items.source_explanation: Total pay is 10,000 + 7,200 = Rs 17,200. F11 describes a combination of time based pay plus incentives for higher performance as a direct payment plan. B and C ignore part of the pay, and D misclassifies direct pay as indirect.
